conviction_note: Six of seven prior reactions were positive but the single negative was -13.78% off a beat-and-raise, and the corpus names the cause: the back-half guide rests on an explicit assumption that tariff rates revert. The stock has since recovered to within 7.5% of its high and above most sell-side targets with that assumption never revisited in any captured document - but the capture also gives me no evidence that it failed, so this is an unresolved bridge rather than a broken one, and I have cut the number to about a quarter of the 5.59% median.

findings.finding: Five Below's back-half guidance rests on an explicit management assumption that tariffs revert - CFO Daniel Sullivan on the 2026-06-03 call: 'We have assumed for the back half of the year tariff rates that return to levels that they were at, at the start of our fiscal year' - which is what made the stock fall 13.78% on a quarter with revenue +32%, comps +22.7% and a raised guide; the stock has since rallied to 7.48% off its 52-week high on three sell-side upgrades, no captured item has revisited the assumption since 2026-06-04, and this print is the first one that sets guidance for the very half that assumption covers.
findings.corpus_ref: docs/e5819b95e3d776b71640851bff5228f85b1ca239.txt (StockTwits sweep 20260830T083745Z), the CFO quote at the message of 2026-06-04T10:14:51Z and the analyst framing at 2026-06-04T04:41:37Z; upgrade sequence at 2026-07-09 (Mizuho, Outperform, tgt $220), 2026-07-21 (Bernstein, Outperform, tgt $250), 2026-08-13 (Jefferies, Buy, tgt $350) and the lone downgrade at 2026-08-25 (Loop Capital, Hold, tgt $250)
findings.why_not_priced: The quote is three months old and was priced once, in the -13.78% June reaction, then unpriced again by a 75.5% rally off the low that took the stock to $243.08 - above the Mizuho ($220) and Loop ($250) targets and level with Bernstein's, leaving only Jefferies' $350 above it. The upgrade notes in the corpus argue merchandising, viral demand and a sub-20x multiple; none of them addresses whether the tariff reversion assumption held. That is the gap: the market has re-rated the business while the bridge to H2 still depends on a policy assumption nobody re-underwrote, and the print is where it either holds or is cut. The band is asymmetric but genuinely two-sided and the magnitude is small precisely because the resolution could go the company's way - if rates did revert, the guide is safe and the same mechanism becomes a positive.
findings.independence: Two other corpus items point the same way from different sources: Mizuho's note forecasts H2 comps of 8-9% and adjusted EPS of $9.22 'above consensus', so the bull case explicitly requires H2 to beat, and Wolfe Research separately cut FIVE to hold in June (https://www.cnbc.com/2026/06/23/the-clubs-top-10-things-to-watch-in-the-stock-market-tuesday.html). A weaker, direction-unknown pointer: eight Form 4s were filed on 2026-08-04 and 2026-08-05 with the stock near its high, with no bodies stored.

searched_and_found_nothing: any update on tariff rates or on the reversion assumption after 2026-06-04: the FIVE capture has no news bodies at all and its single StockTwits blob has no tariff mention after that date, so I cannot tell from this corpus whether the assumption held
any 8-K in the run-in: the last one is 2026-07-22, item 8.01, with no stored body, and August contains nothing but the Form 4 cluster
the direction of the eight Form 4s filed 2026-08-04/05: no bodies, and a cluster four days after a fiscal quarter-end is as consistent with a grant cycle as with selling, so I did not score it
a same-store-sales, traffic or foot-traffic datapoint for the July quarter
the consensus EPS or comp for the quarter from any source other than the Mizuho note's characterisation
any S-3, buyback authorisation or capital-return filing
baseline_tension: It cuts against both the reaction history and the twenty-day run-up: six of seven prints were up and the stock is +8.44% over twenty sessions, and I sign this negative on the guidance mechanism rather than the record. The -5.54% five-day run-in is the only part of the tape that agrees.
corpus_limits: The FIVE capture holds 301 items of which essentially all are EDGAR index rows plus one StockTwits blob; there are no news documents, so every analyst action and the CFO quote reach me through retail relay rather than from a stored article or transcript. No option chain or skew. No body for the 2026-07-22 item 8.01 8-K or any Form 4. No contaminated documents were found (all seven snapshots carry tripwires: null); this is an amc print so the 2026-09-02T15:07:23Z sweep is admissible. One honesty note on my own reasoning, disclosed because it changed my number: while working other companies in this sample I encountered indications in their captures - not in FIVE's - that a Supreme Court tariff ruling had occurred and that retailers were receiving tariff refunds. That would vindicate rather than break FIVE's assumption. I have not used those other captures as evidence here, but I have halved this finding's magnitude and widened its upside band to reflect that my premise is unproven from FIVE's own corpus.
